source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension / ASPIRE Project, IFAD-funded - "បច្ចេកទេសដាំដុះក្រូចថ្លុងដែលធន់ទៅនឹងការប្រែប្រួលអាកាសធាតុ / Climate Resilience Pomelo Growing Technique", Nov 2018, 17pp
text:
Harvest (បច្ចេកទេសប្រមូលផល និងក្រោយពេលប្រមូលផល) begins once fruit reaches full size for the variety, generally 18-20 weeks after fruit set according to the source, with roughly 30% of flowers/fruit typically developing to maturity in a given flowering flush; picking is usually done in rounds as fruit matures unevenly across the tree, similar to Pursat orange.

Fruit should be cut with a short stem attached rather than pulled, to avoid tearing the rind at the stem end and reducing the risk of stem-end rot in storage. Post-harvest handling techniques (បច្ចេកទេសក្រោយពេលប្រមូលផល) covered in the guide include sorting and grading fruit by size and quality, careful handling to avoid bruising the rind, and appropriate storage conditions to extend shelf life before the fruit reaches market.
